commits.message:
feat(renderer): a settings click writes no file: each write lands as a change the host performs, and undo is guarded per setting (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

A writer builds the text it would leave, and the click lands the changes
from the text it read through its turn: the turn answers with the change,
and the change's effect-done turn carries the click on, so a click hears
how each write landed before its reload or next write. A write enters the
undo history only once it landed. Undo, redo and cancel land the
difference between a step's texts, so a hand edit to a setting the step
changed refuses it by name, and an edit elsewhere in the file is kept.
A lint rule leaves the atomic writer to the host's side.

feat(daemon): the host performs a config change a turn returns, and the renderer hears how it landed before the turn is answered (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

A change names its layer by role. The host finds the user layer's file from
the newest request it holds of the session, by the same derivation the
render's resolution names as home, splices the changes in, and refuses the
whole change when a setting it read has moved. Refused is its own outcome,
apart from a write that failed.

feat(config): a config write is a list of changes at addresses, each carrying what it read, and applying them refuses a setting that moved (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

config-changes derives the changes between two documents and applies them
back byte for byte, both ways, over the json5 editor's new address-level
set and remove. A value travels as its JSON5 text, so a copied row keeps its
comments and undo restores the bytes it found; an object whose member
changes would not rebuild it as written is set whole. Spec section 7 says a
change carries text.

refactor(click): load-config and toolbar-toggle are deleted, so a session's config is only what its client named (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

No draw emits either verb. A load-config pick stored an absolute path in
session state and let a click redirect which file a session reads and
writes, so the renderer's home and the file the host will write could
disagree. With the pick gone, no click moves a session's origin, and the
render cache's follow, the views port and the pick's config-target source
go with it. A session uses another file through --config or
CC_CANDYBAR_CONFIG.
docs(spec): A-1's open item says a request waits for the renderer's thread, not for turns taken one at a time (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.cwq) (#767)
